# MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists — facts

> Source-anchored units about MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists: 20 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How it works

- [statement] COMT inhibition reduces levodopa conversion to 3-O-methyldopa and increases levodopa availability; it is an adjunct mechanism that depends on levodopa treatment. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=a511a531-112e-43f8-a43f-5334b0efe979&type=display
- [statement] Safinamide and opicapone can cause or worsen dyskinesia when added to levodopa; both US labels state that reducing levodopa or another dopaminergic drug may mitigate it. (medium confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=a511a531-112e-43f8-a43f-5334b0efe979&type=display
- [statement] Istradefylline is an adenosine A2A receptor antagonist used in the US label as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa for adult OFF episodes; its precise therapeutic mechanism is unknown. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/getFile.cfm?setid=a7d008cb-b273-4049-a5d2-9c6902910d58&type=pdf · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The US XADAGO label uses safinamide as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa for OFF episodes: start at 50 mg once daily, with an increase to 100 mg once daily after two weeks according to need and tolerability; doses above 100 mg have no demonstrated added benefit. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Entacapone is given as 200 mg with each levodopa/decarboxylase-inhibitor dose; its short duration adds dosing burden, and reported adverse effects include diarrhea, urine discoloration and dyskinesia. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] The US ONGENTYS label recommends opicapone 50 mg once daily at bedtime, without food for one hour before and at least one hour after; moderate hepatic impairment reduces the dose to 25 mg, and severe hepatic impairment calls for avoiding use. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=a511a531-112e-43f8-a43f-5334b0efe979&type=display · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] The US NOURIANZ label recommends istradefylline 20 mg once daily, with a possible increase to 40 mg; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cap dosing at 20 mg, and strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/getFile.cfm?setid=a7d008cb-b273-4049-a5d2-9c6902910d58&type=pdf · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Selegiline and rasagiline can provide modest symptomatic benefit as monotherapy in early Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] ADAGIO found a possible disease-modifying signal at 1 mg/day but not 2 mg/day and urged caution, while the clinical review reports that long-term follow-up did not confirm disease modification. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19776408/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Safinamide adjunct trials support reduced OFF time and increased ON time without troublesome dyskinesia; the MDS review describes benefits around one hour compared with placebo, although individual trials vary. (medium confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Selegiline and rasagiline inhibit MAO-B irreversibly, whereas safinamide inhibits it reversibly. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Safinamide inhibits MAO-B and thereby reduces dopamine catabolism; additional effects on glutamate release and sodium channels have been described, but their added clinical relevance remains uncertain. (medium confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/
- [statement] Rasagiline reduces OFF time as an adjunct; the MDS review describes placebo-adjusted reductions of 0.5–0.9 hours/day and rates it likely efficacious, while noting that the average OFF-time improvement did not meet its clinical-meaningfulness threshold. (medium confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/
- [statement] The MDS review found insufficient evidence for selegiline specifically as treatment of motor fluctuations despite attempted optimal oral levodopa therapy, citing small samples, low-quality evidence and heterogeneous results; this conclusion is scoped to that indication. (low confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Entacapone and opicapone act peripherally, while tolcapone crosses the blood–brain barrier and inhibits COMT centrally as well as peripherally. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Opicapone has placebo-controlled evidence for reducing OFF time; the MDS review found no significant PDQ-39 improvement in its included trials. (medium confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/
- [statement] Tolcapone’s practical role is restricted by potentially fatal liver injury and the need for regular liver-function monitoring; the clinical review describes its use after inadequate response or intolerance to other COMT inhibitors. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Safinamide has drug-specific interaction restrictions: its US label contraindicates other MAO inhibitors, including linezolid, selected opioids such as tramadol, SNRIs and certain other antidepressants, and dextromethorphan; SSRIs instead require the lowest effective dose and monitoring for serotonin syndrome. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Istradefylline’s non-dopaminergic receptor target does not eliminate dyskinesia or psychiatric adverse effects: the US label warns of worsened dyskinesia and hallucinations and advises against treatment in major psychotic disorders. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/getFile.cfm?setid=a7d008cb-b273-4049-a5d2-9c6902910d58&type=pdf · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Evidence assessments differ for istradefylline: the MDS motor-fluctuation review rates it likely efficacious while noting inconsistent effects of unclear clinical relevance, whereas EMA’s Nouryant refusal assessment found efficacy insufficiently established. These attributed judgments should not be collapsed into a universal efficacy or availability claim. (medium confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists · also: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/nouryant
